# Leaf spring leaf removal for ride tuning

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove the heavy overload and shorter leaves from the topmost leaf to reduce stiffness. [t140]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Identify the topmost leaf as number 1.
2. Remove the heavy overload leaf (the thickest, straightest one) to reduce stiffness and prevent inversion under extreme load.
3. Remove shorter leaves from the pack starting with #3 or #5 depending on desired ride height.

_Procedure reported by [t140]._

## Specifications

- **Overload leaf weight**: 23 lbs [t140] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Keep longer leaves and remove shorter ones to soften the spring rate according to physics. [t140]
- [Partial] Removing leaves lowers ride height; expect a drop from 3 inches to roughly 2 inches if removing #3, #5, and overload. [t140]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Keeping all short leaves which makes the pack stiffer than intended. [t140]
